_primary_source_identifiers_as_recorded_.citation: Bangerter et al. 2023, Hum Cell — ex-vivo drug sensitivity in patient-derived EMC models USZ20-EMC1 and USZ22-EMC2.

_ceiling_that_must_travel_with_every_use: The reported outcome is an ORDINAL BAND, not a value. Verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:48): "Drug sensitivities were classified as (i) none, (ii) low to moderate and (iii) good to high." The paper computes AUC and IC50 and prints neither in the text for any compound.
The 40-drug screen ran on ONE model (USZ20-EMC1). The second model (USZ22-EMC2) never saw PU-H71 or HDM201.

PU-H71 and HDM201 were NOT validated. Only carfilzomib, doxorubicin and venetoclax went to dose-response; the screen's ordinal band for these two compounds has never been reproduced by any second experiment in the paper.

The one compound whose screen band WAS tested against validation and failed is venetoclax: 'moderate sensitivity' in the screen, and verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:48) "there was no response to venetoclax as a monotherapy in the validation". The screen's ordinal bands are therefore known to be falsifiable in this exact assay pair.

The screen dose range tops at 200 umol/l (Methods, PMC9813045.txt:37); the validation tops at 10 uM. With no printed AUC or IC50, a 'good sensitivity' band cannot be placed on a concentration axis and is not distinguishable from activity far above any achievable exposure.
No normal-cell or non-tumour comparator appears anywhere in the paper. There is no therapeutic index and none can be derived.
Replicate count for the SCREEN is not stated. The validation is explicitly 'in triplicates'; the screen is not.
No clinical exposure of any kind. This is ex vivo only.

5 of 40 compound identities are in the accessible record; 35 are in Fig. 2a/b only. The response matrix is not deposited (data availability: 'available from the corresponding author on reasonable request').

routes.verdict_precision: This is NOT 'the negative is wrong'. The expression result (p53 transcriptional output reads lower in EMC on both platforms, ART-CENSUS-ROUTE-GRADING) is untouched and this patch does not contest one number in it. What fails is the UNSTATED SECOND STEP: that low p53 transcriptional output implies an MDM2/MDM4 antagonist is inactive in this disease. That step was never tested and two readings now bear against it. This is the 'reached without reading a relevant source' case, sharpened to the inference rather than the measurement.

proposed_add_to_supporting_evidence.what_it_supports: HDM201 (MDM2/MDM4) is one of two targeted agents called best-performing in an ex-vivo EMC model. Verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:48): "PU-H71 (HSP90) and HDM201 (MDM2/MDM4) performed best from the compounds tested and showed good sensitivity while the cells had a moderate sensitivity to venetoclax." ⛔ READ THE CEILING: an ORDINAL BAND on n = 1 model (USZ20-EMC1), UNVALIDATED, no AUC or IC50, no comparator, no concentration anchor, no clinical exposure. It is a signal to look further and nothing more. It does not support efficacy and cannot be read as one.
proposed_add_to_supporting_evidence._direction: against the route's current terminal negative, not in favour of the route's premise

proposed_add_to_supporting_evidence.what_it_supports: The screened model carries the class's selecting lesion by the authors' own annotation. Verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:45): "The copy number profiles exhibited gains mainly in chromosome 1, where the MDM4 locus is located, and in chromosome 8, where MYC is located for USZ20-EMC1." ⛔ THIS IS A BROAD CHROMOSOME-1 GAIN THAT THE AUTHORS ANNOTATE FOR THE MDM4 LOCUS. It is NOT a focal MDM4 amplification call, carries no copy-number value, and the same paragraph reports "a rather flat CNV plot for both models". Do not restate it as 'MDM4 amplified'.

proposed_add_to_remaining_unknowns: ⛔ TP53 STATUS REMAINS UNKNOWN AND THIS EVIDENCE DOES NOT CHANGE THAT. The strings TP53 and p53 appear ZERO times in the cached full text of PMC9813045 (grep -c -i, 29 246 bytes). An MDM2/MDM4 antagonist's activity is conditional on TP53 status, so an HDM201 response in a p53-null model would mean something entirely different. ⚠ An absent reading is not a reading of absence: do NOT infer wild-type TP53 from the body text's silence, and do NOT let the HDM201 band imply a p53-dependent mechanism the data cannot support.

★ THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION EXISTS AND IS $0, WHICH FALSIFIES THIS ROUTE'S OWN timing.rationale. Bangerter Supplementary file1 (PDF 89 KB, linked from doi 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x, CC BY open access) is Supplementary Table 1, the FoundationOne®HEME variant list for both models — verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:45): "Details about these alterations are listed in the Supplementary Table 1." ⚠ SCOPE IT HONESTLY: that table lists alterations DETECTED, not the panel's gene list, so it can establish 'no TP53 alteration detected on a hybrid-capture panel of up to 406 genes' and cannot by itself establish wild-type. That is still strictly more than the current UNKNOWN, and it costs nothing.

Whether the screen's ordinal band for HDM201 survives a dose-response validation, which the paper never ran for this compound. The one band that was tested this way (venetoclax, moderate) did not survive.

routes.route_display_name_as_recorded: Chaperone dependency of the chimera (HSP90 and co-chaperones)
routes.verdict: CITE IT, DO NOT PROMOTE ON IT. The grade ◐ PARTLY SUPPORTED stands unchanged, and the addition is smaller than S52 framed it.
routes.verdict_precision: ⛔ S52 §4.2 argues that a direct EMC observation is "a different and better kind of evidence" than the Ewing transfer. That is right about the DISEASE and wrong about the KIND. This route's own clientship artifact already defines the category and grades it: research/literature/fet-fusion-chaperone-clientship-2026-08-27.json:18, key d_fusion_driven_line_sensitive_to_an_HSP90_inhibitor, verbatim: "ABUNDANT, AND IT IS THE WEAKEST CATEGORY. ... Sensitivity of a fusion-driven line is not clientship of the fusion". Bangerter's PU-H71 result IS category (d). Moving a category-(d) observation from Ewing to EMC does not change its category, and by the route's own written standard category (d) cannot reach the route's premise, which is a binding question. ⚠ AND ON RIGOUR IT IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO: the Ewing PU-H71 item in that same artifact carries an immunoblot/RPPA readout of fusion-protein depletion (verbatim: "Exposure to PU-H71 resulted in depletion of critical proteins including AKT, pERK, RAF-1, c-MYC, c-KIT, IGF1R, hTERT and EWS-FLI1 in Ewing cell lines"); Bangerter carries an unvalidated ordinal viability band on n = 1 with no protein readout at all.

proposed_add_to_supporting_evidence.what_it_supports: The route's compound has a direct ex-vivo reading in THIS disease rather than only in Ewing sarcoma. Verbatim (PMC9813045.txt:48): "PU-H71 (HSP90) and HDM201 (MDM2/MDM4) performed best from the compounds tested and showed good sensitivity". ⛔ CATEGORY (d) BY THE ROUTE'S OWN TAXONOMY — a fusion-driven line sensitive to an HSP90 inhibitor — which that taxonomy calls the weakest category and explicitly distinguishes from clientship. An ORDINAL BAND on n = 1 model, unvalidated, no AUC, no normal-cell comparator, no concentration anchor. It does not answer the clientship premise, supplies no therapeutic index, and cannot distinguish tumour need from general need.
proposed_add_to_supporting_evidence._strength_note: Deliberately NOT 'direct'. It is direct on disease and indirect on premise, and the premise is what the route is graded against. Grading it 'direct' would let a viability band stand in for a binding measurement.
